description:
Single edits to the agent org chart. For building or reorganising a whole org use apply_org_plan instead — it is one atomic call rather than many.

Actions:
- set_parent   — move one agent or department under another. Pass parentId: null to unplace it. Cycles are rejected.
- create_department — one new group.
- set_context  — write the shared standards on a department. THIS is what makes the org do something: every agent beneath inherits this text. Draft it from what you can observe about the user's work, show it to them, and let them correct it before you write it. Good content is the instruction they would otherwise repeat to every agent in the group — conventions, definition of done, what to avoid, when to escalate.
- set_resources — attach LIBRARIES, SKILLS and expected MCP servers to a department. Everyone beneath inherits them.
- set_boundaries — declare where agents beneath must STOP, and which libraries they may WRITE to.
- clear        — ⚠️ DESTRUCTIVE AND IRREVERSIBLE. Deletes EVERY department, placement, boundary and attachment in the workspace. There is no undo. NEVER call this without the user explicitly asking to delete their whole org chart in this conversation — "start over", "reset", or an org that looks wrong are NOT sufficient. Tell them exactly what will be lost (how many departments and placements) and get a clear yes first. Agents themselves are not deleted.

RESOURCES vs CONTEXT — the difference matters:
  context   is the RULE. "Follow the design system; never hardcode a hex value."
  resources are the THING. The design system library itself.
A rule that points at a library the agent cannot reach is just a name. Attach both.

Attaching a library makes it REACHABLE, never pasted into a prompt — so attaching is cheap and does not bloat context.

MCP servers are DECLARATIVE ONLY. Contextium cannot grant one: they run in the host (Claude Code, Cursor, ChatGPT). Declaring "Design uses Mobbin" means an assistant can tell the user it is missing and the CLI setup-* commands know to configure it — it does not switch it on. Say so plainly rather than implying the agent now has the tool.

childId.description: set_parent: id of the agent/department being moved

mcpRequirements.description: set_resources: MCP servers this role is expected to have. Declarative — not granted.

slug.description: Marketplace slug if it came from there

parentId.description: set_parent: new parent id, or omit/null to unplace

projectIds.description: set_resources: library (project) UUIDs everyone beneath can reach. Replaces the current list.

skillIds.description: set_resources: skill file UUIDs inherited by everyone beneath. Replaces the current list.

stopConditions.description: set_boundaries: short, concrete conditions where an agent must STOP and escalate instead of proceeding, e.g. "changes billing or pricing", "deletes anything", "publishes externally". Keep them checkable, not vague. These UNION down the chain and can never be removed by anything beneath.

writeProjectIds.description: set_boundaries: library UUIDs agents beneath may WRITE to. Reach (projectIds) is separate from authority — this is authority. INTERSECTS down the chain: nothing beneath can widen it.

name: manage_org
